items.definition:
to go without; to give up
I decided to forgo dessert to save calories.

firmly fix or establish (a habit, belief, or attitude) in a person's mind
The values of hard work were ingrained in him from an early age.

to scatter or spread (things) untidily over a surface or area
Leaves were strewn across the path after the strong winds.

to absorb and integrate (people, ideas, or culture) into a wider society or culture
Immigrants often try to assimilate into their new culture.

to reduce in extent or quantity; impose a restriction on
The new policy will curtail government spending.

to disappear or cause to disappear
The fog began to dissipate as the sun rose.

to give pleasure or satisfaction to
Seeing the project finally completed gratified the team.

infringe
Copying copyrighted material can infringe on intellectual property rights.

to change gradually in shape or form
The caterpillar will morph into a butterfly.

to destroy completely
The bombing raid obliterated the entire city.

extend beyond or above a surface
A sharp rock protruded from the ground.

lead (an attack or movement); be the leader of.
She was chosen to spearhead the new marketing campaign.

depict or treat in a mannered and nonrealistic style.
The artist chose to stylize the figures in her painting.

occur; happen; (of a secret, etc.) be revealed.
It later transpired that the information was false.

stop doing something
The police ordered the protesters to desist from blocking the road.

to bring about or initiate (an action or event)
He was accused of trying to instigate a rebellion.

to censor or obscure parts of a text
The document was heavily redacted before its release.

attribute something to (a cause, source, or author)
He ascribed his success to hard work and a bit of luck.

to complete or make perfect
They hoped to consummate the deal by the end of the week.

to place in a shrine or sacred place; to preserve
The constitution enshrines the rights of citizens.

to be an omen of
The dark clouds bode ill for our picnic.

to give up power or territory
The country was forced to cede territory after the war.

to spread or disperse widely
The organization aims to disseminate information about healthy living.

to issue or spread out from (a source)
A strange light seemed to emanate from the old house.

To honor as holy or sacred.
We hallow the memory of those who died for freedom.

To make someone appear guilty of a crime or wrongdoing.
His testimony could incriminate the suspect.

To overwhelm (someone) with things or people to be dealt with; to flood.
We were inundated with applications for the new position.

to make someone so frightened that they are unable to move or think
The sudden noise petrified the small child.

To prevent from happening; make impossible.
His injury will preclude him from playing in the final.

To fill a place with sound; to be heard loudly.
The hall resounded with laughter.

to shorten by cutting off the top or end
The data was truncated to fit the display.

To leave (property) to a person or other beneficiary by a will.
He bequeathed his entire estate to his niece.

to shock or excite (someone) into taking action; to coat (iron or steel) with a protective layer of zinc
The urgency of the situation galvanized the team into action.

revoke, cancel, or repeal (a law, order, or agreement)
The company decided to rescind its offer of employment.

to reduce or take away the worth or value of
His rude comments did not detract from the overall success of the event.

to persuade someone not to take a particular course of action
We tried to dissuade him from quitting his job, but he was determined.

to feel about blindly or uncertainly
He had to grope in the dark for the light switch.

to gradually but firmly establish (an idea or attitude) in a person's mind
Parents try to instill good values in their children.

to make (an argument, statement, or theory) unsound or invalid
New evidence could invalidate the previous findings.

to state, affirm, or assert something about the subject of a sentence or argument
The theory is predicated on extensive research.

to put an end to (a rebellion or other disorder), typically by the use of force
The police were called to quell the disturbance.

to cut off the head of
In ancient times, it was common to decapitate traitors.

to embody in flesh; to represent in a concrete form
The character incarnates evil.

to cause (an event or situation, typically an undesirable one) to happen suddenly, unexpectedly, or prematurely
The economic crisis precipitated a change in government policy.

to extract metal from its ore by heating
Ancient civilizations learned to smelt copper from its ore.

clear (someone) of blame or suspicion
The new evidence helped to vindicate her reputation.

to make known by open declaration; to proclaim
The government sought to promulgate new laws to protect the environment.

to regain (something lost or spent)
The company hopes to recoup its losses by increasing sales.

To destroy completely.
The army sought to annihilate the enemy forces.

arrange (laws or rules) into a systematic code.
They decided to codify the new regulations to make them clearer.

To adjust or regulate.
The speaker learned to modulate her voice to keep the audience engaged.

to combine or unite to form one organization or structure
The two companies decided to amalgamate to create a stronger entity.

to declare invalid (an official agreement, decision, or result)
The court decided to annul the marriage.

disturb the composure of; unsettle
His sudden appearance disconcerted everyone.

extract (information) from various sources; gather (leftover grain)
From various sources, I was able to glean a few facts about the incident.

to promote or spread (something undesirable)
Some politicians tend to monger fear among the public.

to produce and release a substance
Glands in the skin secrete sweat to cool the body.

to undermine the power and authority of an established system or institution
The rebels tried to subvert the government.

to express severe disapproval of (someone or something), especially in a formal statement
The committee voted to censure the senator for his misconduct.

to unite in a federation
The states decided to federate to form a stronger nation.

to fill with passion or strong emotion
His speech was designed to impassion the crowd.

to think out or plan (an action, especially a crime) beforehand
The crime was clearly premeditated.

to present (something) in a different way; to give a new form to
The director decided to recast the role with a different actor.

to express disapproval or disappointment to (someone)
He reproached her for her carelessness.
